sections.html:
Find Mauldin in Greenville County, with Greenville to the northwest and Simpsonville to the southeast. Its area is about 12.13 square miles, almost entirely land. One county covers the entire city, so Greenville County is the office that assesses your house, collects your tax and records your deed.

U.S. Route 276 (Main Street) runs through the center, 8 miles from Greenville and 5 from Simpsonville. Interstate 385 hugs the eastern side, linking to Interstate 85 to the north and Interstate 185 to the south. That road network puts residents within easy reach of jobs across the Greenville area.

Residents numbered 22,889 in 2010 and 24,724 in 2020, with 31,465 estimated for 2025. Only 5.0% of the 10,808 housing units were empty in 2020.

sections.h2: Permits for repairs before a sale
sections.html:
Permits are the job of the city's Business and Development Services office, phone (864) 234-3475. The permit page covers new residential construction, additions and accessory structures, decks, roofs, demolition, trades work and floodplain development. It also offers a zoning permit, a temporary use permit and an encroachment permit.

Roof and deck permits are the ones most owners fixing up a house will need. You can pay with cash, check or a card. A single fee schedule PDF lists the charges, and the office can quote the one that fits your job.

Running a business from the property is a separate matter, since the city wants a license for any business operating there. A new business pays a $15 review fee, a home occupation pays $25 and renewals fall due April 30.

Greenville County sends your tax bill, typically in the last days of October. January 15 is the payment deadline, and it doubles as the final day to contest the prior year's value.

Selling changes the math for whoever buys next. A qualifying sale counts as an assessable transfer of interest, so the county revalues the house at market as of December 31 in the year of sale and the old 15% cap stops protecting it. Any deed signed by December 31 hits the following year's bill, which is why the county urges owners to record promptly after signing.

The lower 4% ratio is for owner-occupied homes and requires an application. The county wants it by January 15, either postmarked or delivered by hand that day. State law punishes a wrong claim: an owner found ineligible pays at the 6% ratio, plus a penalty equal to 100% of the tax paid and 0.5% interest each month.

When a value goes up, for example after a transfer or new construction, the notice normally lands in late summer or early fall. You then have 90 days to appeal.

Miss January 15 and state law starts adding charges: 3% right away, 7% more after February 1, 5% more after March 16. Penalties like these can cloud the title, so settle what you owe before you close. When something is still outstanding at the table, your closing attorney can pay it out of your sale proceeds. Ask the county treasurer for a current payoff amount rather than guessing, because the total changes with the date.

The Register of Deeds for Greenville County holds your file. Go to Suite S-2100 of Greenville County Square, 301 University Ridge, Greenville, any weekday between 8:30 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., though documents brought in person should arrive before 4:30 p.m. The number is 864-467-7240.

The staff images each document as soon as it is recorded and sends the original back. Plan to pay in cash, by check or by card. Mail filers include a cover letter, a return envelope with postage and a check.

Recording a deed triggers a transfer fee of $1.85 per $500 of value, divided as $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. Exemptions exist for a deed given to a lender in lieu of foreclosure and for a corrective deed that merely confirms title already held. The clerks are not allowed to advise you on the law, so a legal professional should prepare the deed.

sections.h2: Why Mauldin owners look at cash sales
sections.html:
Owners here reach for a cash sale for a handful of reasons, and several of them overlap.

  • A house with repairs that a buyer's lender would insist on
  • An inherited home whose heirs live elsewhere
  • A rental that has a tenant or sits empty
  • A deadline from a job change, a move or a tax bill

Cash Home Buyers looks at Mauldin houses in their present shape, including those needing roofs, decks or other work the city would permit. A seller does not have to finish that work first, though it is smart to know which items would have needed a permit.

Compare the offer with a regular listing before you choose. A listing may bring a higher price on paper, but it also brings showings, a buyer's inspection, repair requests and the chance that financing falls through at the last minute. Weigh the extra weeks of mortgage, tax and utility payments against that possible gain.

sections.h2: What a purchase looks like step by step
sections.html:
You start by describing the property. We study it as it sits today and, when it fits what we buy, mail or email an offer that spells out how we reached the figure. Turning it down costs nothing.

No lender means no appraisal to clear, and you pick the day. The title company or closing attorney searches the title, pays off liens and unpaid tax out of your proceeds, then files the deed with Greenville County.

Gather these before we talk: the newest tax notice, a payoff statement if a loan is open, and permit records for roofs, decks or additions. An estate house also needs the papers that name the person allowed to sign.

Plan the move-out too. Schedule the final walk-through, take photos of the house's condition and keep every closing document for your tax records. After closing, cancel your utilities and homeowner insurance and send the county your new mailing address so later notices find you.

faqs.q: What county is Mauldin, SC in?
faqs.a: Mauldin is in Greenville County. The county assesses the property, bills the tax and records the deed through its Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: When are Greenville County property taxes due on a Mauldin house?
faqs.a: Payment is due by January 15, after bills mail around the end of October. Late balances take a 3% penalty first and further penalties after February 1 and March 16.

faqs.q: Does a sale change the property tax on a Mauldin home?
faqs.a: For the next owner it does. The county revalues a qualifying sale at market value as of December 31 of that year and drops the 15% cap. A buyer who will live there has to apply separately for the 4% rate.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Mauldin house?
faqs.a: The Greenville County Register of Deeds takes it, at Suite S-2100, 301 University Ridge in Greenville. Expect the $1.85 per $500 state fee. Drop-offs in person should come before 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to fix my Mauldin house before selling?
faqs.a: Frequently. Roofs, decks, additions and demolition all have their own permit forms at City of Mauldin. Call Business and Development Services and describe the project.
